newsitem.title: USA: Orange County considers $200 mln refunding.
newsitem.headline: Orange County considers $200 mln refunding.

text.p: Orange County, Calif. is considering the sale of about $200 million in debt to refund outstanding pension obligation bonds.

Richard Meister, a vice president with Goldman Sachs & Co said the County Board of Supervisors has authorized its finance staff to review the proposed issuance to refund $192 million of outstanding taxable bonds.
Meister said MBIA Insurance, a unit of MBIA Inc, has agreed to insure the proposed debt.
"We do not expect there to be a market penalty on these bonds," he said.
County Supervisors are expected to consider the bond proposal later this month.
Orange County declared bankruptcy in December 1994 and emerged from bankruptcy last June.
Meister is part of the team that has worked on Orange County's recovery borrowings.
He spoke to reporters after giving a presentation at the Bond Buyer's public finance conference here.
